segments.speaker: Guest

segments.en: Like I guess surely at University campus libraries, sometimes people are sneakily taking a nap.

segments.speaker: Guest

segments.en: But it's not really so publicly accepted, I would say, to do that.

segments.speaker: Guest

segments.en: So I'm just wondering, Andrew, have you ever seen people sleeping at the library or on the bus or anywhere else in Korea?

segments.speaker: Guest

segments.en: What's the deal over there?
segments.ko: 거기는 어떤가요?
segments.speaker: Guest

segments.en: Well, Indiana, first, I should say, that I loved a library nap when I was a university student between classes.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: I always took a nap.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: Now, I wouldn't say it's totally super rare to see someone sleeping or napping on a bus or subway back in North America, but I think there's a lot less trust among people in society.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: So for me personally, I don't think I'd ever want to totally pass out on the subway, maybe be like in Toronto or something if I were back in Canada, because I'd be worried somebody's going to steal my phone while I'm sleeping or maybe somehow get to my wallet and take my wallet.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: So I wouldn't want to not be paying attention in that way.

segments.speaker: Host

segments.en: But here in Korea, and I think the same thing happens in Japan as well, it's a higher trust society.
